newsitem.title: USA: China buys US soybeans, meal, oil in Nov 7 wk - USDA.
newsitem.headline: China buys US soybeans, meal, oil in Nov 7 wk - USDA.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Department said Friday China bought 249,800 tonnes soybeans in the week ended Nov 7 and 54,200 tonnes soybean meal.
In its weekly export sales report, USDA also said China bought 10,000 tonnes soybean oil.
It said China's soybean purchases included new sales of 99,500 tonnes and changes in destination of 150,300 tonnes.

So far this marketing year, China has imported 322,100 tonnes of U.S. soybeans, compared with 79,500 tonnes at this time last year. Oustanding sales of U.S. beans to China total 525,800 tonnes, compared to zero outstanding sales the same period a year ago. Total commitments of U.S. soybeans to China now stand at 847,800 tonnes, compared to only 79,500 for the same period last year, and more than double China's total purchases of U.S. soybeans in 95/96.

Exports of U.S. soybean meal to China are also running way ahead of normal. USDA statistics show that China has so far this year imported 79,200 tonnes of U.S. bean meal, compared to zero for this time last year. Oustanding sales to China total 346,500 tonnes. Last year China only bought 90,000 tonnes of U.S. soybean meal.

U.S. soybean oil exports to China total 44,000 tonnes so far this year, compared to 22,000 this time last year. Outstanding sales total 4,500 tonnes, versus 30,000 last year, and total commitments of U.S. soybean oil sales as of Nov 7 were 48,500 tonnes, compared to 52,000 for the same period this year. Last year China bought 135,300 tonnes of U.S. bean oil.
